corrections.comment: Checked the reply against every tool and agent result in the run. None mentions Ancestry, FindMyPast or archives, yet the reply recommends all three, plus an unsupported claim that Schuylkill County records are "sparse on FamilySearch… for Irish immigrants". The test says to mark down a site no tool returned. The rest (project made, empty profile, empty search) is accurate.

Made the project with init-project, then ran the record search in the same turn, with no question, plan or locality survey. It reported the empty result honestly, left out init-project's next-step sentence, and ended on a "Continue with …?" offer. All validators pass.
person_read used LZNY-BRF as the fixture expects, and project_create used the right person ID. Every call matched a fixture or live tool, with no fixture_not_found.

Checked the reply against every tool and agent result. "Ancestry, FindAGrave, or Pennsylvania newspaper archives" appear in none of them; the test says to mark down a site no tool returned. Schuylkill County itself is fine: it's Patrick's death place in the profile and the search report. The rest is accurate.

Made the project with init-project, then ran the record search in the same turn, with no question, plan or locality survey. It reported the empty result honestly, left out init-project's next-step sentence, and ended on "Continue with running the searches?". All validators pass.
person_read and project_create both used LZNY-BRF as the fixture expects, and project_context used the right project path. Every call matched a fixture or live tool, with no fixture_not_found.

The narration is honest but shows internal ids: log_017, the hit id 3Q9M-CSK3-ZSLR, and the agent name record-structurer. The test (JC3) requires narration free of internal ids. Milder than it looks, since the "Continue" message carried the same ids, but still against the test's rule.

Accepted "Continue" and handed hit 9 of log_017 to record-structurer, without re-judging the hit or offering the step again. The run ends at the stubbed hand-off by design, and the hand-off check (test_search_hit_review_yes_extracts_the_matches) passes.
Only project_list and project_context were called, both live, with the right project path. No arguments were expected, and there was no fixture_not_found.

Research didn't activate, and the main thread wrote nothing (no file changes), so no plan was created, as required. The facts are right: q_001's plan items are all completed, the probate search was empty, and ps_001 has no claims (the engine's own flagged finding). But "You are not done planning" is wrong for a resolved question whose search is stopped, and it suggests adding a Thomas Flynn census plan item, which the test says not to volunteer. Not a 1: JC1 allows answering directly or declining to plan.
project_context plus research_query for q_001's plans and log, all live with the right arguments. No fixture_not_found.

The test wants the planning question sent to research-plan without an inline strategy (JC1), and the main thread wrote one anyway. It also has errors: it gives Patrick's birthplace as Pennsylvania (the tree says Ireland), and it pushes browsing Thomas Flynn's probate for a will when the project already holds his 1881 will (src_006).

Research didn't activate and nothing was handed to research-plan, so the routing JC1 calls ideal never happened. The no-browse, no-write invariant held: no volume_search or image_search call, and no file changes. That's why the test passes.
project_context plus research_query for plans and the log, all live with the right arguments. No fixture_not_found.

Checked the calls and the reply. project_context returned no_project, and the narration says so accurately: "No project yet — initializing one for Patrick Flynn (LZNY-BRF)". LZNY-BRF is the ID the user gave, not an internal id. Nothing invented.

The bare first message activated research, which handed off to init-project first with the user's message verbatim and the project path. test_routes_to_expected_skill passes. The run stops at the stubbed hand-off by design, so no summary is expected.
project_list with no arguments, then project_context with the working folder's path, both live. No fixture_not_found.

Checked the reply against the stub. All 11 verdicts are relayed as the stub gave them, and every hit being an identical Match is the stub's design (JC1), not an error. It judged nothing itself and extracted nothing. Minor: the closing "new vital information" slightly overstates the stub's "a detail the tree does not have yet".

11 evaluate-search-results spawns, one per hit of log_017 (test_search_hit_review_spawns_one_agent_per_hit passes). All verdicts came back in one turn with no stop between batches, and it ended on "Continue with extracting the 11 Matches?". The judge's own rationale concludes "Score is 3 on reflection… Adjusting to 3" but left 2.
project_list first with no arguments, then project_context with the folder's path, then sidecar_read on results/log_017.json#hits, all correct. No fixture_not_found.

The narration is accurate (both censuses give birth ~1832, in the assertions) but shows internal ids to the user: src_005, a_014–a_016, src_006, a_017–a_019, and "@plugin:person-evidence". JC4 requires none. It also flags the 13-year gap before handing off, leaning toward the inline judgment JC2 warns against, though it doesn't give a verdict.

Handed the same-person question straight to person-evidence, with the user's words verbatim and the assertion ids, without walking the job routing table. test_routes_to_expected_skill passes. The run stops at the stubbed hand-off by design.
project_list first with no arguments, project_context with the folder's path, then research_query for the assertions on src_005 and src_006, all live with correct arguments. No fixture_not_found.

Checked the narration against the scenario: one open question, one planned item (the Hamre baptism, christened 7 April 1759, 1757–1761), and no evidence yet. Accurate, with no internal ids shown. Mildly repetitive (the search line appears twice), which isn't a factual issue.

Read the plan and the subject's tree facts, then handed off to search-records with the plan item verbatim. test_routes_to_expected_skill and test_delegation_hands_plan_item_verbatim both pass. It ended on "Continue with running the searches?".

project_list, project_context, research_query for q_001's plans, and tree_query on LKFW-9XH (the subject's id in this tree) for birth, christening, death and marriage facts, all live and correct. No fixture_not_found.

It shows internal ids (src_005, src_006) to the user, against the test's rule. The judge's "factual misstatement" is wrong, though: src_005 and src_006 are the 1870 and 1880 Schuylkill censuses. Minor: "b. ~1845 PA" takes the objective's birthplace over the tree's (Ireland), the same slip as 016.

Treated the doubt as a same-person question and handed it straight to person-evidence, quoting the researcher's words exactly ("I'm not sure the Patrick Flynn… born in Pennsylvania about 1832"). test_person_evidence_spawn_carries_the_users_words and test_routes_to_expected_skill pass. It didn't answer the question itself.
project_list first with no arguments, then project_context with the folder's path, both live. No fixture_not_found.

Checked the narration against the calls. Objective but no questions, no attached FamilySearch records for I1, an empty timeline, then question-selection. All accurate, with nothing invented about prior research.

Followed the "Objective but no questions" row: extraction_append, then timeline_build for I1, then question-selection, on the listed project, not a new one. test_named_subject_continues_the_listed_project, test_no_init_project_on_existing_project and test_routes_to_expected_skill all pass.

It recovered: project_list, then project_context on /proj_3f9a1c2e7b4d6a80, then extraction_append and timeline_build with the right project and person I1.

Checked the narration against the scenario: one open question (Anders Monsen's parents), one planned item (Hamre baptisms 1757–1761, the 7 April 1759 christening), and no evidence yet. Accurate and honest about what was handed off. Minor: it shows "q_001" and "subject block" to the user, which the house style discourages, but this test doesn't grade it.

Read the active plan and the subject's facts, then handed off to search-records with the plan item verbatim. test_routes_to_expected_skill and test_delegation_hands_plan_item_verbatim both pass. It ended on "Continue with running the searches?".

project_list, project_context, research_query (plans, q_001, active), and tree_query on LKFW-9XH (the subject's id here) for birth, death and christening facts, all live and correct. No fixture_not_found.

Checked the reply against the calls. There are no attached records for Patrick Flynn, so extraction and the timeline returned nothing, and it says so. It describes the question-selection hand-off as what it was for, not as a question already written (the stub changed nothing). Minor: it shows tool names and "I1", which the house style discourages but this test doesn't grade.

One step this turn, as the test requires: extraction_append and timeline_build for I1, then question-selection, ending on "Continue with setting up the project?". test_routes_to_expected_skill and test_spawn_carries_its_step_mode_fields (userPresent: no on an autonomous run) both pass.
project_list, project_context, then extraction_append and timeline_build with the right project path and personId I1, all live. No fixture_not_found.

It correctly sees the record contradicts h_002 (a man who died in 1861 can't marry in 1870) and repeats the reported facts as given. But it adds an origin the researcher never stated: "James Eastham of Virginia origin". That comes from an 1880 census note about Polley Burton's father, whose link to the Easthams is unproven, and it isn't labelled as an inference (JC1). The judge's "claimed action never performed" is wrong: hypothesis-tracking is stubbed, and the reply says it "was asked", not that it was done.
project_list, project_context, then research_query for hypotheses and conflicts, all live with the right project path. No fixture_not_found.

It answered both halves of the question: the probate nil needs no new plan item, and the real next step is proof-conclusion to add ps_001's claims. JC1 accepts answering directly instead of routing to research-exhaustiveness. The stray plan suggestion is scored under Correctness, not twice.

Its next step is locating the death record itself, in Kentucky Deaths and Burials (1843–1970), a collection a tool returned, covering Pulaski County in 1861. JC3 counts that as following the lead, and it doesn't jump to wrapping up. Every callee is stubbed, so writing nothing is expected; JC4 says not to grade the hand-off.
